aspect: EXAMPLE - the announcement and the number
description: Petrol was 219.03 naira per litre before removal. A year later the average retail price had more than doubled to 655.48 naira - a 199.26% increase in twelve months. Daily consumption fell from about 66.9 million litres to 48.43 million.
energy_note: Two hundred and nineteen naira, then six hundred and fifty-five.

description: Transport costs surged by close to 300%, with direct knock-on effects on the cost of essential food commodities, because in Nigeria food price is largely a transport price.
Headline inflation rose from 22.41% in May 2023 to 22.79% in June, then 31.70% by February 2024 and 34.19% by June 2024.
energy_note: A third of the value of everything, in a year.

aspect: The World Bank's estimate of who it pushed under
description: The World Bank warned that if conditions persisted an additional 4 million citizens would likely join the 133 million already in multidimensional poverty.
energy_note: Four million more, on top of a hundred and thirty-three.

description: The subsidy had become fiscally unsustainable at over N1 trillion annually and was associated with corruption and smuggling. Removal created fiscal space, curtailed smuggling and accelerated reform. Both things are true; only one of them is experienced at a market stall.
energy_note: A defensible policy, paid for by people with no margin.

aspect: Palliatives did not reach the gap
description: Cash transfers and a compressed-natural-gas initiative were introduced; critics describe them as insufficient and poorly targeted, which is the ordinary fate of a transfer programme in a country with an incomplete identity system.
energy_note: Compensation that requires a database nobody finished.

description: The fare to her shop went from NGN 300 to NGN 900 across eight months. Her margin did not move. By the fourth month she is walking part of it; by the sixth she is opening four days a week instead of six.
energy_note: A business shrunk by the cost of getting to it.
